question: How many days of holidays do full-time staff get each year?
answer: Full-time employees receive 23 days of annual leave per year, plus Irish public holidays. After five years of continuous service this rises to 25 days.

question: Does my holiday entitlement go up the longer I stay?
answer: After five years of continuous service this rises to 25 days. Up to five unused days may be carried over into the first quarter of the next leave year.

question: When do I need a doctor's note if I'm off sick?
answer: Book through the customer portal or by phoning the service desk. One-off visits need at least 48 hours' notice.
citations: customer_faq § How do I book a cleaning visit?

question: Is it enough to email my manager when I'm too ill to come in?
answer: After passing probation, employees receive full pay for up to 10 days of certified sick leave in any rolling 12-month period, in addition to statutory sick pay. Employees must phone their line manager before 09:30 on the first day of absence; a text or email alone is not sufficient.

question: How long is the trial period for new hires?
answer: New employees serve a six-month probation period. Probation may be extended once by up to three months.

question: Can I work from home, and how often?
answer: After probation, office-based staff may work remotely for up to two days per week, agreed with their manager. Site-based roles are not eligible for remote working.

question: How much notice do I have to give if I resign after my probation?
answer: During probation either side may end employment with one week's notice. After probation the notice period is four weeks, or the statutory minimum if that is longer.

question: What time do I have to be at work by?
answer: The standard working week is 39 hours, Monday to Friday. Core hours are 10:00 to 16:00; outside core hours staff may start between 07:30 and 10:00 and finish between 16:00 and 19:00 by agreement with their line manager.

question: How long do I have to put in a claim for money I spent on a work trip?
answer: All expense claims are submitted through the SpendDesk portal within 30 days of the expense being incurred. Claims submitted later than 30 days will only be paid with written approval from the Finance Manager.

question: Who has to sign off a claim of 800 euro?
answer: Line managers approve claims up to 500 euro. Claims above 500 euro also require approval from the Finance Manager.

question: What is the rate per km for driving my own car for work?
answer: Use of a private car on company business is paid at 0.43 euro per kilometre for the first 1,500 km in a calendar year and 0.26 euro per kilometre after that. Commuting between home and your normal place of work is not claimable.

question: Can I claim for a pint with dinner on a business trip?
What's the maximum I can spend on a hotel in Dublin?
answer: Overnight stays must be booked through the travel desk. The nightly cap is 140 euro in Dublin and 110 euro elsewhere in Ireland, including breakfast.

question: Who is allowed a company credit card?
answer: Company credit cards are issued to managers only. Personal use of a company card is a disciplinary matter, even if repaid.

question: How long must my password be?
answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long. Passwords are not changed on a fixed schedule; they must be changed immediately if a compromise is suspected.

question: Do I have to change my password every 90 days?
answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long. Passwords are not changed on a fixed schedule; they must be changed immediately if a compromise is suspected.

question: I left my laptop on the train - who do I tell and how fast?
Can I copy files to a memory stick?
What should I do with a dodgy-looking email?
answer: Suspicious emails must be reported using the Report Phishing button in Outlook, or by forwarding to security@brightwater.example. Do not click links or open attachments in a suspected phishing email.

question: How long are server backups kept?
answer: Critical security patches are installed within 72 hours of release; other patches within 14 days. File server backups run nightly at 01:00 and are retained for 35 days.

question: How quickly will you respond if our site floods?
answer: For P1 incidents Brightwater will respond within 1 hour and aim to resolve or make safe within 4 hours. P3 requests receive a response within 2 business days and are scheduled into the next planned visit.

question: What compensation do we get if you miss an emergency response time?
answer: If a P1 response target is missed, the client receives a service credit of 5 percent of the monthly fee for each breach, capped at 25 percent of the monthly fee in any month. Service credits are the client's sole financial remedy for missed targets.

question: During what hours is the normal service available?
answer: Standard service hours are 07:00 to 19:00, Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. A 24/7 emergency line is available for Priority 1 incidents only.

question: Do the targets still apply during a red weather warning?
answer: Targets do not apply to faults caused by the client's own contractors, to access delays caused by the client, or during declared severe weather warnings (Met Eireann orange or red).

question: How long is security camera footage kept?
answer: CCTV footage is kept for 30 days and then overwritten, unless it is needed for an investigation. Accident report forms are kept for 10 years.

question: How long do you have to reply when someone asks for a copy of their personal data?
answer: Anyone may ask for a copy of the personal data Brightwater holds about them. Requests are answered within one month of receipt; this can be extended by two further months for complex requests, in which case the requester is told within the first month.

question: When must a data breach be reported to the regulator?
answer: Any suspected personal data breach must be reported to the DPO immediately. Where required, the breach is notified to the Data Protection Commission within 72 hours of Brightwater becoming aware of it.

question: Where do we gather if the fire alarm goes off?
answer: On hearing the fire alarm at the Galway office, leave by the nearest exit and go to the assembly point at car park B. Fire wardens carry out a roll call at the assembly point.

question: Do I need permission before going up a tall ladder?
answer: Any work at a height above 2 metres requires a working-at-height permit signed by a supervisor before work starts. Ladders must be inspected before each use.

question: How often should someone on their own at a site check in?
answer: Staff working alone on a site must check in through the SafeShift app every 2 hours. If a check-in is missed, the supervisor phones the worker; if there is no answer within 15 minutes the escalation procedure starts.

question: Which counties do you work in?
answer: We provide contract cleaning, maintenance and facilities services in counties Galway, Mayo, Clare and Roscommon.

question: What happens if I cancel the cleaners the morning of the visit?
answer: Cancellations are free up to 24 hours before the scheduled start. Later cancellations are charged at 50 percent of the visit price.

question: How much is an emergency callout at the weekend?
answer: Out-of-hours callouts are charged at 85 euro per hour with a minimum charge of 2 hours, plus materials.

question: When is payday?
answer: Salaries are paid monthly by credit transfer on the 25th of each month, or the previous working day if the 25th falls at a weekend. You can join the company pension scheme after six months; Brightwater matches employee contributions up to 5 percent of salary.

answer: Bring photo ID and your PPS number. IT will issue your laptop and set up MFA on your first morning.

question: Who is the chief executive of Brightwater?

answer: Employees may take up to five days of paid bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member, and up to two days for an extended family member.
